title: Scaling a Vue Codebase
learning_outcomes: Explain the optional specialist topic “Scaling a Vue Codebase” in a JavaScript-first Vue project.
Identify the contract or code-organization problem the technique is intended to solve.
State the tooling/runtime assumptions and one limitation.

content.intro: This lesson studies Scaling a Vue Codebase within TypeScript and Large-Scale Code Organization. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Types can make component contracts more explicit, but they add tooling and should fit the needs of the project and team.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: TypeScript is an optional specialization for larger Vue codebases; the core teaching path and repository files remain JavaScript/JSX. This lesson focuses on Scaling a Vue Codebase. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: Feature-based folder structures
items.text: For Feature-based folder structures, connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: Component, service, and store boundaries
items.text: For Component, service, and store boundaries, define one source of truth and separate stored state from derived values and actions. Avoid duplicating the same fact in component-local state and a global store; persist only what the product genuinely needs.

items.title: Module naming and import conventions
items.text: For Module naming and import conventions, connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: Shared types and utilities
items.text: For Shared types and utilities, TypeScript is a recommended specialization rather than a prerequisite for the JavaScript path. Use types to make component contracts and external data assumptions explicit, and keep runtime validation for values received from an API.

content_blocks.expected_output: Each folder expresses a responsibility: reusable UI, route views, reusable reactive logic, shared state, API boundaries, navigation, and app composition.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Adapt this outline to project size; prefer cohesive feature boundaries over empty folders or overengineering.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Scaling a Vue Codebase with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “Component, service, and store boundaries”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: TypeScript is an optional specialization for larger Vue codebases; the core teaching path and repository files remain JavaScript/JSX. For Scaling a Vue Codebase, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: TypeScript is an optional specialization from the supplied PDF. The CodeLeaf repository patch remains JavaScript/JSX-only and adds no .ts/.tsx files. A TypeScript snippet is illustrative and requires a separate Vue project with language tooling. Runtime validation is still needed for API data.

content.task: Create a small example for “Scaling a Vue Codebase” that applies “Feature-based folder structures”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “Feature-based folder structures”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.

summary: Scaling a Vue Codebase belongs to the broader area TypeScript and Large-Scale Code Organization.
The main concept to practice is Feature-based folder structures.
Verify a normal result and one meaningful boundary case before using the pattern in a production feature.
